label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2009
detail: CRA table lists $5,000 for each of 2009 to 2012.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2010
detail: CRA table lists $5,000 for each of 2009 to 2012.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2011
detail: CRA table lists $5,000 for each of 2009 to 2012.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2012
detail: CRA table lists $5,000 for each of 2009 to 2012.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2013
detail: CRA table lists $5,500 for 2013 and 2014.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2014
detail: CRA table lists $5,500 for 2013 and 2014.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2015
detail: CRA table lists $10,000 for 2015 only.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2016
detail: CRA table lists $5,500 for each of 2016 to 2018.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2017
detail: CRA table lists $5,500 for each of 2016 to 2018.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2018
detail: CRA table lists $5,500 for each of 2016 to 2018.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2019
detail: CRA table lists $6,000 for each of 2019 to 2022.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2020
detail: CRA table lists $6,000 for each of 2019 to 2022; the CRA registered plan limits table agrees.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2021
detail: CRA table lists $6,000 for each of 2019 to 2022; the CRA registered plan limits table agrees.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2022
detail: CRA table lists $6,000 for each of 2019 to 2022; the CRA registered plan limits table agrees.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2023
detail: CRA table lists $6,500 for 2023. Note: one worked example on CRA's Calculate your contribution room page mislabels 2023 as $7,000; the limits tables say $6,500.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2024
detail: CRA table lists $7,000 for each of 2024 to 2026.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2025
detail: CRA table lists $7,000 for each of 2024 to 2026.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2026
detail: CRA table lists $7,000 for each of 2024 to 2026; the CRA registered plan limits table also shows $7,000 for 2026.

label: TFSA annual dollar limit 2027
value: not yet published
detail: The CRA registered plan limits table lists TFSA dollar limits only up to 2026 as of October 22, 2026. Figures on private websites (for example $7,500) are estimates, not CRA figures.

label: Cumulative TFSA room 2009 to 2026 (eligible since 2009, never contributed)
detail: Sum of the CRA annual limits for 2009 to 2026, for someone who was 18 or older and resident in Canada every year since 2009 and never contributed. CRA does not print this total; it is calculated from CRA's verified annual limits.

label: How the TFSA limit is set
value: Indexed to inflation, rounded to the nearest $500
detail: CRA states the TFSA dollar limit is indexed to inflation and rounded to the nearest $500.

label: Who can open a TFSA
value: Resident of Canada for tax purposes, 18 or older, valid SIN
detail: All three conditions must be met to open a TFSA. Banks, insurance companies, credit unions and trust companies can issue TFSAs.

label: Opening a TFSA where the age of majority is 19
value: Open at 19; room from the year you turned 18 carries over
detail: In some provinces and territories you must be 19 to enter a contract such as a TFSA. Once the person turns 19 they can open a TFSA and carry over the room from the year they turned 18.

label: Provinces where the age of majority is 18
value: Alberta, Manitoba, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Quebec, Saskatchewan
detail: Federal sources list 18 as the age of majority in these six provinces. IRCC's Studying in Canada as a minor page shows the same list.

label: Provinces and territories where the age of majority is 19
value: British Columbia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Northwest Territories, Nova Scotia, Nunavut, Yukon
detail: Federal sources list 19 as the age of majority in these seven jurisdictions. IRCC's Studying in Canada as a minor page (canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/prepare/minor-children.html) shows the same list.

label: When TFSA room starts
value: Year you turn 18
detail: For residents, contribution room starts to accumulate when you turn 18. The annual limit for the year you turn 18 is included in full.

label: TFSA room for newcomers to Canada
value: Room starts the day you become resident; only years of residency count
detail: A newcomer aged 18 or older starts accumulating room on the day they become resident. CRA's example: a person who became resident in 2024 had only the 2024 limit of $7,000, not the cumulative limits since 2009.

label: TFSA limit in the year of arrival or departure
value: Full annual limit, no proration
detail: CRA states that if you are a resident for part of the year, you receive the full annual dollar limit as contribution room for that year.

label: TFSA room in years of non-residence
value: No new room for a year in which you are non-resident
detail: No new annual room accrues for a year you are a non-resident. Amounts withdrawn while non-resident are added back to room only once you become resident again.

label: Tax on TFSA contributions made while non-resident
detail: Contributions made while non-resident (other than qualifying transfers or exempt contributions) are taxed at 1% for each month they remain, until withdrawn or until you become resident again. If the contribution also exceeds your room, a separate 1% monthly excess tax applies.

label: TFSA withdrawals while non-resident
value: Not taxed in Canada
detail: Withdrawals made while non-resident are not taxed in Canada, but you cannot re-contribute tax-free until you are resident again.

label: How TFSA room is calculated
value: Current year limit + unused room + prior-year withdrawals - contributions this year
detail: Unused room carries forward indefinitely. Withdrawals do not change the current year's room.

label: When TFSA withdrawals are added back to room
value: January 1 of the following year
detail: Amounts withdrawn are added back as new room on January 1 of the next calendar year, at the same time as the new annual limit.

label: Tax on TFSA over-contributions
detail: Any excess is taxed at 1% per month on the highest excess amount in each month it remains. There is no grace amount, unlike the RRSP $2,000 cushion.

label: TFSA return filing deadline when tax is owed
value: June 30 of the following year
detail: Withdraw the excess as soon as possible, then file the TFSA Return and pay by June 30 of the following year.

label: Holding more than one TFSA
value: Allowed; one combined room limit
detail: Your contribution room is the total you can contribute to all your TFSAs combined.

label: Qualified TFSA investments
value: Money, GICs and deposits; most securities listed on a designated stock exchange (shares, warrants, options, ETF and REIT units); mutual and segregated funds; Canada and provincial savings bonds; debt of listed corporations; investment-grade debt; insured mortgages
detail: CRA says permitted TFSA investments are generally the same as those permitted in an RRSP.

label: Tax on non-qualified TFSA investments
detail: A non-qualified investment is taxed at 50% of its fair market value when acquired or when it became non-qualified. Income and gains on it are taxable to the trustee, and income not withdrawn promptly may attract the 100% advantage tax.

label: Tax on prohibited TFSA investments
detail: A prohibited investment is one closely connected to the holder, for example a significant interest (10% or more) in a company. It is taxed at 50% of FMV, and income or gains on it attract the 100% advantage tax.

label: Refund of the 50% tax
value: Possible if disposed of by the end of the following calendar year
detail: The 50% tax may be refunded if the investment is disposed of, or stops being non-qualified or prohibited, before the end of the calendar year after the year it was taxed. No refund if the holder knew or should have known; the 100% advantage tax is never refunded.

label: TFSA advantage tax
detail: An advantage is a benefit or debt conditional on the TFSA's existence, or a transaction that artificially shifts value into or out of the TFSA. Any advantage is taxed at 100%.

label: Frequent trading inside a TFSA
value: Income may be taxed as business income
detail: CRA states that TFSA holders who invest with the frequency and experience of a professional trader may have their account deregistered and any income earned taxed as a business. CRA gives no numeric trade-count test.

label: TFSA successor holder
value: Surviving spouse or common-law partner only
detail: The successor holder immediately becomes the new holder and the TFSA keeps its tax-free status; their own room is not affected if the deceased's TFSA had no excess. CRA notes Quebec does not recognize successor holder designations for TFSAs.

label: TFSA designated beneficiary
value: Tax-free up to FMV at death; later earnings taxable
detail: A designated beneficiary (a spouse not named as successor, family member, other person or organization) pays no tax on amounts up to the TFSA's FMV at death. Earnings after the date of death are taxable.

label: TFSA exempt period after death
value: Ends December 31 of the year after the year of death
detail: The exempt period ends at the end of the first calendar year that begins after the death, or earlier if the trust ends. A trust that continues after that becomes a taxable inter vivos trust.

label: Survivor exempt contribution deadline
value: By December 31 of the year after death; Form RC240 within 30 days
detail: A surviving spouse or partner can contribute a payment from the deceased's TFSA to their own TFSA without using room if done by December 31 of the year following death, filing Form RC240 within 30 days of contributing.

label: Direct transfer between TFSAs
value: No effect on contribution room
detail: Ask the receiving institution to do a direct transfer; the amount moved does not affect your room.

label: Withdraw then redeposit instead of transferring
value: Counts as a new contribution
detail: CRA warns against withdrawing and recontributing yourself: it is not a direct transfer, the redeposit uses room, and the withdrawal is only restored the next calendar year, which can cause an over-contribution.

label: TFSA transfer on separation or divorce
value: Direct transfer does not affect either person's room
detail: Qualifies only if the partners live separate and apart and the transfer follows a court order or written separation agreement.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2020
detail: From the CRA table of registered plan limits.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2021
detail: From the CRA table of registered plan limits.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2022
detail: From the CRA table of registered plan limits.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2023
detail: From the CRA table of registered plan limits.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2024
detail: From the CRA table of registered plan limits.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2025
detail: From the CRA table of registered plan limits; CRA's deduction limit page also states $32,490 for 2025.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2026
detail: From the CRA table of registered plan limits. Your personal limit is the lesser of this and 18% of 2025 earned income, adjusted for pension adjustments and unused room.

label: RRSP dollar limit 2027
detail: Published by CRA: the 2027 RRSP dollar limit equals the 2026 money purchase limit of $35,390.

label: RRSP deduction limit formula
value: Lesser of 18% of prior-year earned income and the annual RRSP dollar limit, minus PA and PSPA, plus PAR, plus unused room
detail: CRA calculates your limit from 18% of your earned income in the previous year, capped at the annual dollar limit, less your pension adjustment and past service pension adjustment, plus any pension adjustment reversal and unused room carried forward.

label: Unused RRSP room
value: Carries forward
detail: Unused deduction room from prior years is added to your limit. Contributions you make but do not deduct can also be deducted in a later year.

label: RRSP contribution deadline rule
value: 60th day of the following year
detail: The RRSP contribution year begins on the 61st day of a year and ends on the 60th day of the following year.

label: RRSP contribution deadline for the 2025 tax year
detail: CRA: March 2, 2026 was the deadline for contributing to an RRSP for the 2025 tax year.

label: RRSP contribution deadline for the 2026 tax year
value: not yet published
detail: CRA has not yet posted the 2026 tax year deadline. Applying CRA's 60th-day rule gives Monday, March 1, 2027, but publish that date only once CRA confirms it.

label: RRSP over-contribution cushion
detail: Excess contributions are amounts above your deduction limit plus $2,000. You qualify for the $2,000 only if you were 18 or older at any time in the previous year.

label: Tax on RRSP excess contributions
detail: Tax of 1% per month applies to the excess above the limit plus $2,000. File Form T1-OVP within 90 days after the end of the calendar year; a waiver can be requested on Form RC2503 for a reasonable error.

label: Last day to contribute to your own RRSP
value: December 31 of the year you turn 71
detail: December 31 of the year you turn 71 is the last day you can contribute to your own RRSP.

label: RRSP options in the year you turn 71
value: Withdraw, transfer to a RRIF, or buy an annuity
detail: Withdrawals have tax withheld; amounts transferred directly to a RRIF have no tax withheld and are taxed later as RRIF payments are received.

label: Spousal RRSP contributions after you turn 71
value: Allowed until the end of the year your spouse or partner turns 71
detail: T4040 (Rev. 25): you can contribute to an RRSP where your spouse or common-law partner is the annuitant until the end of the year they turn 71.

label: Spousal RRSP attribution rule
value: Contributions in the withdrawal year or either of the two preceding years
detail: If you contributed to your spouse's or partner's RRSP in the year of withdrawal or either of the two preceding years, you (the contributor) will generally include the withdrawal in your income. Use Form T2205.

label: Exceptions to spousal RRSP attribution
value: Not itemized here
detail: Exceptions exist (see Form T2205), but the CRA pages fetched did not list them, so none are recorded as verified.

label: RRSP lump-sum withholding, outside Quebec, up to $5,000
detail: Withholding on RRSP lump-sum withdrawals of $5,000 or less for residents outside Quebec.

label: RRSP lump-sum withholding, outside Quebec, $5,001 to $15,000
detail: Withholding on RRSP lump-sum withdrawals over $5,000 up to $15,000 for residents outside Quebec.

label: RRSP lump-sum withholding, outside Quebec, over $15,000
detail: Withholding on RRSP lump-sum withdrawals over $15,000 for residents outside Quebec.

label: RRSP lump-sum federal withholding, Quebec, up to $5,000
detail: Federal withholding for Quebec residents on withdrawals of $5,000 or less. Quebec provincial tax is also withheld on top.

label: RRSP lump-sum federal withholding, Quebec, $5,001 to $15,000
detail: Federal withholding for Quebec residents. Quebec provincial tax is also withheld on top.

label: RRSP lump-sum federal withholding, Quebec, over $15,000
detail: Federal withholding for Quebec residents. Quebec provincial tax is also withheld on top.

label: Quebec provincial withholding on RRSP lump sums
value: Not verified
detail: CRA confirms provincial tax is also withheld in Quebec and refers to Revenu Quebec, but the provincial rate was not confirmed on a Revenu Quebec page in this pass.

label: RRSP withholding for non-residents
detail: Withholding is 25% for non-residents of Canada unless reduced by a tax treaty.

label: Pension adjustment (PA) basics
value: Reduces next year's RRSP room
detail: A PA is your total pension credits for the year with a specific employer. It reduces what you can contribute to an RRSP and PRPP in the next year; it can be zero but never negative.

label: Home Buyers' Plan withdrawal limit
detail: CRA: currently the HBP withdrawal limit is $60,000 in total per participant.

label: Effective date of the $60,000 HBP limit
value: Withdrawals made after April 16, 2024 (Budget Day)
detail: Budget 2024 raised the limit from $35,000 to $60,000 for withdrawals made after Budget Day (April 16, 2024). CRA's own HBP page states the current $60,000 limit but not the date.
source_name: Department of Finance Canada (Budget 2024, Tax Measures)

label: Previous HBP limit
detail: The limit before the Budget 2024 increase.
source_name: Department of Finance Canada (Budget 2024, Tax Measures)

label: HBP first-time home buyer test
value: No owner-occupied home in the current year (ignoring the 30 days before withdrawal) or the previous four calendar years
detail: You must not have lived in a home you or your spouse or partner owned. The test is waived for a buyer helping a person with a disability and for someone living apart from a spouse or partner after a breakdown.

label: Other HBP conditions
value: Written agreement to buy or build, intend to occupy within one year, Canadian resident at withdrawal
detail: You need a written agreement to buy or build a qualifying home when you withdraw, must intend to occupy it as your principal residence within one year, and must be resident in Canada at the time of withdrawal.

label: Deadline to buy or build the home
value: Before October 1 of the year after the first withdrawal
detail: The qualifying home must be acquired or built before October 1 of the year after the year of the first withdrawal.

label: HBP withdrawal window
value: Same calendar year as the first withdrawal, or January of the next year
detail: Multiple withdrawals are allowed within that window using a separate Form T1036 for each.

label: Recent RRSP contributions and the HBP
value: 89-day rule
detail: RRSP contributions made in the 89 days before an HBP withdrawal may not be deductible.

label: HBP repayment period
detail: You have up to 15 years to repay. The minimum each year is your HBP balance divided by the years remaining (1/15 in the first year).

label: When HBP repayment normally starts
value: Second year after the year of the first withdrawal
detail: This is the standard rule for withdrawals outside the temporary relief years.

label: Temporary HBP repayment deferral (first withdrawals 2022 to 2025)
value: Repayment starts in the fifth year after the first withdrawal
detail: Budget 2024 relief defers the start of repayment by three more years for first withdrawals made January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025. Example: first withdrawal in 2022, first repayment year 2027.

label: Extension of HBP repayment deferral (first withdrawals 2026 to 2028)
value: Extended; repayment starts in the fifth year after the first withdrawal
detail: CRA's HBP page (modified 2026-02-17) says the relief has been extended to first withdrawals made January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2028; a first withdrawal in 2026 means the first repayment year is 2031. CRA's repayment sub-page still shows only the 2022 to 2025 window.

label: If an HBP repayment is missed
value: Shortfall added to income as RRSP income (line 12900)
detail: Repayments can be made in the year due or the first 60 days of the next year; any shortfall is included in income and reduces the HBP balance.

label: Using the HBP and an FHSA for the same home
value: Allowed
detail: You can withdraw under the HBP and make a qualifying FHSA withdrawal for the same qualifying home if you meet all conditions at the time of each withdrawal.

label: Lifelong Learning Plan annual withdrawal limit
detail: You can withdraw up to $10,000 from your RRSPs in a calendar year under the LLP (Form RC96).

label: Lifelong Learning Plan total limit per participation
detail: You cannot withdraw more than $20,000 each time you participate. Withdrawals can continue until January of the fourth calendar year after the first withdrawal, or earlier if repayment starts.

label: Who can use the LLP
value: You or your spouse or common-law partner as the student
detail: The student must enrol full-time in a qualifying program at a designated institution (part-time allowed if disability conditions are met) and the withdrawer must be resident in Canada.

label: LLP repayment
value: 10 years, at least 1/10 a year; starts no later than the fifth year after the first withdrawal
detail: Repayment usually starts earlier if the student stops qualifying. Any shortfall in a year is added to income on line 12900.

label: FHSA annual participation room
detail: Room is $8,000 in the year you open your first FHSA and $8,000 a year after that, subject to the lifetime limit.

label: FHSA lifetime limit
detail: Total contributions and RRSP-to-FHSA transfers over your lifetime cannot exceed $40,000.

label: FHSA unused room carry-forward maximum
detail: Unused room carried forward is capped at $8,000, so the most you can add in one year is $16,000 ($8,000 plus $8,000 carried forward). The $16,000 figure is calculated from CRA's formula.

label: When FHSA room starts
value: Only once you open your first FHSA
detail: Room begins in the year you open your first FHSA; the carry-forward in that year is $0, so no room builds up before you open an account.

label: Who can open an FHSA
value: Canadian resident, 18 or older (19 where that is the legal age), 71 or younger at December 31 of the year opened, first-time home buyer
detail: All conditions apply when the account is opened. You can hold more than one FHSA.

label: FHSA first-time home buyer test (opening)
value: No home owned and lived in by you or your current spouse or partner in the current year before opening or the previous four calendar years
detail: The spouse test only applies if you have a spouse or common-law partner when the account is opened.

label: FHSA maximum participation period
value: Ends December 31 of the year of the earliest of: 15th anniversary of first FHSA, turning 71, or the year after the first qualifying withdrawal
detail: The period begins when you open your first FHSA.

label: FHSA first-time home buyer test (withdrawal)
value: No owned home lived in during the current year before the withdrawal (ignoring the 30 days before it) or the previous four calendar years
detail: This test is applied again at the time of each qualifying withdrawal.

label: FHSA qualifying withdrawal conditions
value: Written agreement to buy or build before October 1 of the year after the withdrawal; home not acquired more than 30 days before; occupy within one year; Canadian resident
detail: The completion date in the written agreement must be before October 1 of the year following the withdrawal, and you must occupy or intend to occupy the home as your principal residence within one year. Use Form RC725.

label: Transferring an FHSA to an RRSP or RRIF
value: Tax-deferred direct transfer; does not use RRSP room
detail: A direct transfer to an RRSP or RRIF does not affect your unused RRSP deduction room, provided you have no excess FHSA amount. Only direct transfers qualify.

label: Tax on FHSA excess amounts
detail: 1% per month on the highest excess FHSA amount in the month until it is eliminated. Remove it by designated withdrawal or transfer (Form RC727), taxable withdrawal, or new room on January 1.

label: Carrying forward FHSA deductions
value: Allowed, even after the FHSA is closed
detail: Contributions are deductible in the year made or a future year. Transfers from an RRSP into an FHSA are not deductible.

label: FHSA contribution deadline
value: December 31; no 60-day period
detail: The contribution period is January 1 to December 31. Contributions made in the first 60 days of a year cannot be deducted for the previous year.

label: FHSA and HBP for the same home
value: Allowed
detail: You can use both for the same qualifying home if you meet all conditions at the time of each withdrawal.

label: If no home is bought
value: Transfer to an RRSP or RRIF, or withdraw as taxable income, before the period ends
detail: Property left after the maximum participation period loses FHSA status and its FMV is included in income for that year.

label: RESP lifetime contribution limit per beneficiary
detail: Lifetime limit across all RESPs for a beneficiary. There has been no annual limit since 2007. Contributions are not deductible.

label: Tax on RESP excess contributions
detail: Each subscriber pays 1% per month on their share of an excess not withdrawn by month-end, payable within 90 days after year-end.

label: Last year for RESP contributions
value: Year that includes the 31st anniversary of the plan
detail: After that year no contributions other than transfers from another RESP can be made (specified plans excepted).

label: When an RESP must close
value: End of the year that includes the 35th anniversary of opening (40th for a specified plan)
detail: If an AIP is paid, the plan must be terminated by the end of February of the year after the first AIP.

label: Family plan rules
value: Multiple beneficiaries, each related by blood or adoption to every living subscriber, under 21 when named
detail: Family plans are the only RESPs that allow more than one beneficiary. Every beneficiary needs a SIN and Canadian residency when designated.

label: Individual (non-family) plan rules
value: Single beneficiary
detail: CRA confirms that only family plans allow more than one beneficiary. The common statement that an individual plan beneficiary can be anyone of any age, including the subscriber, was not found on the CRA pages fetched.

label: CESG basic rate
detail: 20% of the first $2,500 contributed each year, regardless of family income.

label: CESG basic annual maximum
detail: Basic CESG adds up to $500 a year (20% of $2,500).

label: CESG maximum in one year using carry-forward
detail: Unused grant room carries forward; a child can receive up to $1,000 of CESG in a year when unused room exists.

label: CESG lifetime maximum
detail: Maximum CESG per beneficiary, including the additional CESG.

label: CESG age limit
value: End of the calendar year the child turns 17
detail: Contributions after that year do not attract CESG.

label: CESG rules at ages 16 and 17
value: At least $2,000 contributed by the end of the year the child turns 15, or at least $100 a year in any four years before then
detail: Amounts counted must not have been withdrawn. If neither test is met, no CESG is paid at 16 or 17.

label: Additional CESG, lower income bracket (2026)
detail: Extra 20% on the first $500 ($100 a year) when adjusted family net income is below $58,523, for a total of up to $600 a year in CESG.

label: Additional CESG, middle income bracket (2026)
detail: Extra 10% on the first $500 ($50 a year) when adjusted family net income is $58,523 to $117,045, for a total of up to $550 a year in CESG.

label: Additional CESG income threshold 2026 (lower)
detail: Below this adjusted family net income, the extra rate is 20%.

label: Additional CESG income threshold 2026 (upper)
detail: Above this adjusted family net income there is no additional CESG; only the basic 20% applies.

label: Additional CESG income thresholds 2025
detail: CRA's CESG page still shows the 2025 thresholds: under $57,375 (extra 20%) and $57,375 to $114,750 (extra 10%). Use the 2026 ESDC figures for current content.

label: Canada Learning Bond first-year amount
detail: $500 for the first year of eligibility. CRA adds that ESDC pays $25 more with the initial bond to help with RESP opening costs.

label: Canada Learning Bond yearly amount after the first year
detail: $100 for each later year of eligibility, up to and including age 15.

label: Canada Learning Bond lifetime maximum
detail: No personal contributions are required to receive the CLB.

label: Canada Learning Bond eligibility
value: Children from low-income families born in 2004 or later; apply before age 21
detail: The beneficiary must be under 21 when the application is made.

label: CLB income threshold, 1 to 3 children (July 2026 to June 2027)
detail: Adjusted family income of $58,523 or less.

label: CLB income threshold, 4 children (July 2026 to June 2027)
detail: Adjusted family income under $66,036.

label: CLB income threshold, 5 children (July 2026 to June 2027)
detail: Adjusted family income under $73,577. For more than 5 children ESDC says to call 1-800-622-6232.

label: CLB automatic RESP opening
value: From April 2028
detail: The Government of Canada will automatically open an RESP to deposit the CLB for eligible children born in 2024 or later who are not already RESP beneficiaries by age 4. Opt-out requests start in 2027.

label: BC Training and Education Savings Grant
detail: One-time grant for B.C.-resident children born in 2006 or later named in an RESP; no contribution required.

label: BCTESG application window
value: From the 6th birthday until the day before the 9th birthday
detail: The earliest you can request it is when the child turns six; you can apply any day before the ninth birthday.

label: Quebec Education Savings Incentive basic amount
value: 10% of net contributions, up to 250 a year
detail: With unused rights from earlier years, the basic amount can reach $500 in a year.

label: QESI additional amount
value: Up to 50 a year, based on family income
detail: Revenu Quebec states up to $50 a year may be added based on family income. The income thresholds were not shown on the page fetched.

label: QESI additional amount income thresholds
value: Not verified
detail: Not shown on the Revenu Quebec pages fetched.

label: QESI lifetime maximum
detail: Total QESI per beneficiary across all RESPs; ESDC's estimating page shows the same figure.

label: QESI eligibility
value: Under 18, SIN, resident in Quebec on December 31, designated RESP beneficiary
detail: Special requirements apply at 16 or 17, which the page did not spell out.

label: Other provincial RESP grants currently listed
value: None besides QESI and BCTESG
detail: CRA's provincial programs page and ESDC's estimating page list only Quebec (QESI) and British Columbia (BCTESG).

label: EAP limit, first 13 weeks, qualifying (full-time) program
detail: Maximum EAP for the first 13 consecutive weeks in a qualifying educational program (at least 10 hours a week).

label: EAP limit, specified (part-time) program
detail: Maximum EAP for the 13-week period ending at the time of payment in a specified educational program (at least 12 hours a month).

label: Accumulated income payment (AIP) conditions
value: Paid to one Canadian-resident subscriber, and after the year of the 9th anniversary with every beneficiary 21+ and not eligible for EAPs, or in the 35th-anniversary year, or all beneficiaries deceased
detail: Any one of the three timing tests is enough once the residency and single-subscriber conditions are met.

label: Additional tax on AIPs
value: 20 (12 in Quebec)
detail: Charged on top of regular income tax on the AIP.

label: AIP to RRSP transfer limit
detail: Lifetime maximum of AIPs that can be sheltered by contributing to an RRSP in the year received or the first 60 days after, within available RRSP room; Form T1171 waives withholding.

label: RRIF factor formula, age 70 or younger
detail: CRA: if the age is 70 or younger, the prescribed factor is 1 divided by (90 minus the age).

label: RRIF minimum factor age 55
detail: Calculated with CRA's formula 1/(90-55) = 1/35, about 2.86%.

label: RRIF minimum factor age 56
detail: Calculated with CRA's formula 1/(90-56) = 1/34, about 2.94%.

label: RRIF minimum factor age 57
detail: Calculated with CRA's formula 1/(90-57) = 1/33, about 3.03%.

label: RRIF minimum factor age 58
detail: Calculated with CRA's formula 1/(90-58) = 1/32 = 3.125%, shown rounded.

label: RRIF minimum factor age 59
detail: Calculated with CRA's formula 1/(90-59) = 1/31, about 3.23%.

label: RRIF minimum factor age 60
detail: Calculated with CRA's formula 1/(90-60) = 1/30, about 3.33%.

label: How the RRIF minimum is calculated
value: FMV of the RRIF at the start of the year x prescribed factor
detail: The factor uses the annuitant's age at the start of the year, or the spouse's or partner's age if that was elected when the RRIF was set up.

label: When the first RRIF minimum is due
value: The year after the year the RRIF is set up
detail: No minimum is required in the year the RRIF is established.

label: Using a spouse's age for the RRIF minimum
value: Allowed by election
detail: You can elect to base the minimum on your spouse's or common-law partner's age; a younger spouse's age gives a lower minimum. The election is made when the RRIF is set up.

label: Withholding on RRIF withdrawals above the minimum
value: Lump-sum rates on the excess: 10/20/30% (Quebec 5/10/15% federal)
detail: CRA's payer guide treats the part of a RRIF payment above the minimum as a lump sum subject to the 10%, 20%, 30% bands. The guide implies but does not state outright that no tax must be withheld on the minimum itself.

label: Pension income amount (line 31400)
value: Up to 2000
detail: Federal claim is the lesser of $2,000 and eligible pension income. RRIF and RRSP annuity income qualifies at 65 or older; under 65 it qualifies only if received because of a spouse's or partner's death.

label: Pension income splitting
value: Up to 50% of eligible pension income
detail: Both spouses must be Canadian residents on December 31, not living apart, and file a joint Form T1032. RRIF and LIF payments qualify when the transferring spouse is 65 or older at year-end, or if received because of a spouse's death.

label: LIF minimum withdrawal (federally regulated LIFs)
value: Income Tax Act RRIF minimum
detail: Federal pension rules say that if the holder does not choose an amount, the minimum determined under the Income Tax Act is paid from the LIF each year; the same RRIF factors apply.
source_name: Justice Laws Website (Pension Benefits Standards Regulations, 1985, s. 20.1)

label: LIF maximum withdrawal (federally regulated LIFs)
value: Formula cap before age 90; no cap from the year the holder turns 90
detail: Before age 90 the annual maximum is set by a formula (fund balance divided by an annuity factor); from the year the holder turns 90 the whole balance can be paid out.
source_name: Justice Laws Website (Pension Benefits Standards Regulations, 1985, s. 20.1)

label: Provincial LIF maximums and unlocking rules
value: Not verified
detail: Provincially regulated LIFs follow each province's pension law. Ontario's regulation text could not be loaded, so no provincial LIF maximum is recorded.

label: CDIC coverage limit
unit: CAD per category per member institution
detail: Each eligible category is insured separately up to $100,000 including principal and interest, and each member institution has its own coverage.

label: CDIC category: deposits in one name
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Deposits held in one name are one coverage category.

label: CDIC category: joint deposits
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Deposits held in more than one name are insured separately.

label: CDIC category: deposits held in trust
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Deposits held in trust are insured separately.

label: CDIC category: RRSP deposits
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Eligible deposits inside an RRSP are insured separately.

label: CDIC category: RRIF deposits
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Eligible deposits inside a RRIF are insured separately.

label: CDIC category: TFSA deposits
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Eligible deposits inside a TFSA are insured separately.

label: CDIC category: RESP deposits
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Eligible deposits inside an RESP are insured separately.

label: CDIC category: RDSP deposits
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Eligible deposits inside an RDSP are insured separately.

label: CDIC category: FHSA deposits
value: Separate 100000 category
detail: Eligible deposits inside an FHSA are insured separately.

label: What CDIC covers and does not cover
value: Covers deposits in Canadian or foreign currency, GICs and term deposits; not mutual funds, stocks, bonds, ETFs or crypto
detail: Provincially regulated credit unions and caisses are covered by provincial deposit insurance plans instead, according to FCAC.

label: CIPF limit: general accounts (cash, margin, TFSA, FHSA)
detail: $1 million for all general accounts combined, including TFSAs and FHSAs.

label: CIPF limit: registered retirement accounts (RRSP, RRIF, LIF)
detail: A separate $1 million for all registered retirement accounts combined.

label: CIPF limit: RESPs
detail: A separate $1 million for all RESPs combined where the client is the subscriber.

label: What CIPF covers
value: Client property held by an insolvent member firm; not market losses
detail: CIPF covers missing securities and cash if a member firm fails. It excludes drops in value, unsuitable advice, issuer insolvency and crypto assets.

label: Who regulates investment dealers
value: CIRO (Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization)
detail: CIRO is the pan-Canadian self-regulatory organization overseeing all investment dealers, mutual fund dealers and trading on Canada's debt and equity marketplaces. CIPF member firms are CIRO members.

label: US dividend withholding under the Canada-US treaty (portfolio)
detail: Article X(2)(b) caps US tax on dividends paid to Canadian residents at 15% (5% only for a company owning at least 10% of the voting stock). The payer needs a valid Form W-8BEN on file to apply it.
source_name: Department of Finance Canada (Canada-US Tax Convention, consolidated)

label: US withholding without treaty documentation
detail: IRS: most US-source income received by a foreign person is subject to 30% tax unless a treaty reduces it.

label: Form W-8BEN
value: Given to the payer or broker by a foreign beneficial owner
detail: IRS: give Form W-8BEN to the withholding agent if you are a foreign person and the beneficial owner of an amount subject to withholding, including when claiming a reduced rate.

label: Treaty exemption for retirement arrangements
value: Dividends and interest exempt for arrangements operated exclusively to provide pension, retirement or employee benefits
detail: Article XXI(2) exempts dividends and interest earned by a resident trust or arrangement that is generally tax-exempt at home and operated exclusively for pension, retirement or employee benefits.
source_name: Department of Finance Canada (Canada-US Tax Convention, consolidated)

label: Accounts exempt from US dividend withholding
value: RRSP, RRIF and similar retirement accounts (LIRA, LIF)
detail: Canada-US tax treaty Article XXI(2) exempts dividends and interest received by a trust or other arrangement operated exclusively to provide pension or retirement benefits that is generally exempt from tax in Canada. RRSPs, RRIFs and locked-in retirement accounts (LIRA, LIF) are such arrangements, so US-listed securities held directly in them are exempt from US withholding once the broker has the account documented. Status set by the editor (Sharad to confirm).
source_name: Department of Finance Canada (Canada-US Tax Convention, consolidated)

label: Accounts not exempt from US dividend withholding
value: TFSA, RESP, FHSA and non-registered accounts
detail: TFSA, RESP and FHSA are not arrangements operated to provide pension or retirement benefits, so the Article XXI(2) exemption does not apply and the 15% treaty rate (30% without a W-8BEN) is withheld; the tax cannot be recovered as a foreign tax credit inside these accounts. Status set by the editor (Sharad to confirm).
source_name: Department of Finance Canada (Canada-US Tax Convention, consolidated)

label: Foreign tax credit in a non-registered account
value: Credit = lesser of foreign tax paid and Canadian tax on that income
detail: Report the gross foreign income and claim the federal foreign tax credit on Form T2209 (line 40500); outside Quebec claim the provincial part on Form T2036.

label: 15% cap on creditable foreign tax on property income
value: Not verified
detail: The rule that foreign tax on investment income above 15% is deductible rather than creditable was not confirmed on a CRA page in this pass.
